Agriculture Domain - Land Management Regulations

Land management is governed by state land records departments, property registration acts, and water rights regulations.

For Land Records Digitization: Required attributes include owner name, property identifier (survey number, parcel ID), property boundaries (coordinates or survey description), area measurements, existing land use classification, encumbrances (mortgages, liens), and historical ownership chain. Property tax assessment number may be linked.

For Land Ownership Transfer: Required attributes include seller name and identification, buyer name and identification, property identifier, sale price (for stamp duty calculation), transfer deed document, registration fee payment, and witness information. Notarization may be required. Mutation certificate updates land records.

For Land Survey Registration: Required attributes include owner/applicant name, property identifier, survey purpose, surveyor license number, survey measurements and coordinates, boundary markers description, and survey fee payment. Contiguous property owner information may be required for boundary disputes.

For Lease Agreement: Required attributes include lessor (landowner) name and identification, lessee (tenant) name and identification, property identifier, lease duration, lease terms (rent, conditions), and registration fee. Crop sharing arrangements must be documented. Government lease programs may have additional requirements.

For Irrigation Management: Required attributes include landowner/farmer name, property identifier, water source (canal, tube well, etc.), irrigation area, crop types requiring irrigation, and water allocation permits if applicable. Meter readings for billed irrigation water. Contact information for irrigation schedule notifications.

UNNECESSARY Attributes: Religion, ethnicity, income details (unless for means-tested irrigation subsidies) are unnecessary. Social media profiles are not required. Email is optional unless digital notifications are requested.

Property Registration Act governs land transactions. Water rights are subject to state water resource management regulations.

Privacy: Land records are typically public records accessible for title searches, but personal contact information may be redacted in public access systems.
